headline: 155* : West Indies secure record chase to beat India
summary: Skipper Shai Hope overcame a groin injury to smash an unbeaten 155, leading the Windies to a five-wicket victory in the final ODI.
details: West Indies achieved a record-breaking chase of 351 runs to defeat India by five wickets in the final one-day international on Saturday.
Captain Shai Hope was the star of the show, scoring an unbeaten 155 runs despite battling a groin injury and being forced to open the batting.
Hope's innings was highlighted by a ferocious finish, where he smashed 40 runs off his final 16 deliveries to bring home the win with 10 balls to spare.
India had earlier posted a mammoth 351-7, powered by a career-best unbeaten 129 from KL Rahul and a quick-fire 92 from Rohit Sharma.
The Indian side recovered from an early collapse of 4-2, thanks to a large 137-run partnership between Rohit and Ruturaj Gaikwad.
West Indies bowler Jayden Seales provided the early breakthrough, dismissing both Shubman Gill and Virat Kohli in quick succession.
Despite the series win for India (2-1), the Windies captain noted that the chase was a challenge he managed by remembering advice from MS Dhoni on maintaining composure.
Hope was named player of the match for his match-winning century and leadership under pressure.
caption:
A record-breaking chase and a heroic century! Shai Hope battles through injury to lead West Indies to a stunning win over India.

West Indies achieved a record-breaking chase of 351 runs to defeat India by five wickets in the final one-day international on Saturday.

Captain Shai Hope was the star of the show, scoring an unbeaten 155 runs despite battling a groin injury and being forced to open the batting.

Hope's innings was highlighted by a ferocious finish, where he smashed 40 runs off his final 16 deliveries to bring home the win with 10 balls to spare.

India had earlier posted a mammoth 351-7, powered by a career-best unbeaten 129 from KL Rahul and a quick-fire 92 from Rohit Sharma.

The Indian side recovered from an early collapse of 4-2, thanks to a large 137-run partnership between Rohit and Ruturaj Gaikwad.

West Indies bowler Jayden Seales provided the early breakthrough, dismissing both Shubman Gill and Virat Kohli in quick succession.

Despite the series win for India (2-1), the Windies captain noted that the chase was a challenge he managed by remembering advice from MS Dhoni on maintaining composure.

Hope was named player of the match for his match-winning century and leadership under pressure.

headline_marked: Brazil [[cruise to 4-0 win over India]] in friendly match
headline: Brazil cruise to 4-0 win over India in friendly match
summary: Samuel Lino's second-half brace and a goal from Estevao lead the five-time world champions to a dominant victory at Salt Lake Stadium.
details: Brazil secured a dominant 4-0 victory over India in a friendly match on Saturday, with Samuel Lino scoring twice in the second half to seal the win.
Chelsea winger Estevao opened the scoring in the 28th minute with a left-footed strike, before assisting Pedro for the second goal.
Samuel Lino, a 26-year-old Flamengo winger, netted the third goal and then dribbled past two defenders to make it 4-0 just before full-time.
India, ranked 138th in the world, struggled to convert their chances, with Manvir Singh and Ryan Williams failing to find the net.
The match was played before a crowd of 51,000 at the Salt Lake Stadium, where fans cheered both teams with equal enthusiasm.
Brazil coach Carlo Ancelotti experimented with his squad, making eight changes from their previous match against Australia.
The result extends India's winless streak to six matches, as they faced the challenge of a high-powered Brazilian side.
caption:
A 4-0 rout! Brazil's world-class talent proves too much for India in a friendly clash.

Brazil secured a dominant 4-0 victory over India in a friendly match on Saturday, with Samuel Lino scoring twice in the second half to seal the win.

Chelsea winger Estevao opened the scoring in the 28th minute with a left-footed strike, before assisting Pedro for the second goal.

Samuel Lino, a 26-year-old Flamengo winger, netted the third goal and then dribbled past two defenders to make it 4-0 just before full-time.

India, ranked 138th in the world, struggled to convert their chances, with Manvir Singh and Ryan Williams failing to find the net.

The match was played before a crowd of 51,000 at the Salt Lake Stadium, where fans cheered both teams with equal enthusiasm.

Brazil coach Carlo Ancelotti experimented with his squad, making eight changes from their previous match against Australia.

The result extends India's winless streak to six matches, as they faced the challenge of a high-powered Brazilian side.
